notice: Research guidance, not the TypeSafe request schema, a vendor guarantee, or permission to run tools.
framing: Community emergence (including Laya) → abstract structured decision models, positioning and potential value → three-model comparison → separate Jev, NanoJev and Laya deep dives → scenario cards with on-demand plans, two interactive demos with on-demand practice notes, and adoption. Market observations are adjacent demand evidence, not this category's TAM or proof of production gains.
interactive_chapter: Only #jev-arena and #jev-benchmark, each followed by a practice-note card. Former chapter 08 Alternatives is removed; following main chapters are renumbered. Shared API inspection is under #jev-model-lab in Jev integration; NanoJev/Laya retain their own runtime setup and links to the shared gateway.

scenario_selection_ui.behavior: Scenario cards and per-demo note cards open canonical on-demand sources, not repeated main chapters. Popup sources live outside main and carry no slide/reading markers at runtime. Copies strip IDs and controls; old hashes open the corresponding popup, including nested practice anchors. Without JavaScript, a requested hash reveals its source via CSS. No model calls from opening notes.

enterprise_adoption.scope: Vendor-neutral adoption of structured decision models into existing enterprise architecture; former evaluation and assistant-brief chapters are merged. Model-specific runtime instructions remain in model chapters. Recommendations, not a compliance certificate or proven enterprise ROI.

dimensions.topic: Decision inventory, measurable business value, error consequences, reversibility, no-adoption alternative
Existing CRM/ERP/workflows, internal semantic contracts, adapters, policy and authorization, sync/async queues, idempotency and versioned tenant-safe caches
Hosted/local/hybrid tradeoffs, residency and egress, licenses, secret/tenant controls, supply-chain checks and vendor exit
Accountable owners, review capacity, SLOs, differentiated failures, circuit breakers, drift and delayed outcome feedback
Representative labels, independent test splits, critical strata, practical baselines and no-model ablations
Risk-weighted errors, calibration vs confidence, selective coverage, confidence intervals and real business outcomes
Whole-path and lifecycle cost, annotation/maintenance, throughput/tail latency, shadow/canary rollout and full-policy rollback
ADR deliverables, responsible owners, evidence gates, accept/pilot/defer/reject outcomes and explicit execution approval

enterprise_adoption.accounting: Cpre + Cdecision + r*CLLM + h*Chuman + Cretry + Cops; escalation/review can overlap. Include labeling, integration and maintenance; compare at matched quality and count successful outcomes, not just request price.
enterprise_adoption.non_equivalence: Do not treat class distributions, Noul/scalar judgments, confidence and LLM self-scores as identical or use typed output as authorization. Provider/score semantics need explicit versioned mapping.
enterprise_adoption.decision_gate: Adopt only when business value, quality/coverage, risk, review capacity, latency/capacity, data permissions, cost and operational ownership pass together. Otherwise retain the existing workflow, defer or reject.

model_chapter_navigation: Header has exactly one entry for each model: Jev, NanoJev and Laya. Contract/evidence/integration/limits are nested inside Jev; reference integration and local MLX inside NanoJev. Each model has an internal contents navigation; legacy anchor URLs and detailed visible prose are retained.

demand_evidence.hn_windows: Eight complete UTC dates per launch: Jev September 15–22, 2026; Qwen3 April 28–May 5, 2025; GPT-OSS August 5–12, 2025; DeepSeek-R1 January 20–27, 2025; GPT-6 Astra September 3–10, 2026; Claude Opus 5 July 24–31, 2026. D0 is the launch date, not a full 24 hours after announcement.
demand_evidence.version_scope: Named model launches, not whole brands. Generic DeepSeek-only mentions are not automatically counted as R1. GPT-6 Sol/Luna and Opus 5.5 launched September 22 and lack eight dates, so are omitted rather than zero-filled. All original cohorts retained unchanged.
demand_evidence.index_anomalies: Seven GPT-6 and one Opus 5 comments predate their currently indexed parent thread, possibly from merging/reassociation. Preserve comment timestamps and count anomalies separately, not silently repair/drop them.
demand_evidence.hn_scope: Exact-alias submissions in titles/URLs/story bodies, deduplicated by story ID. Count actual in-window reply timestamps on those threads, not current points as historical data. Reposts remain; replies need not repeat the keyword or be positive. Not whole-web/unique-user/market-size evidence. Years, platform size, deletions and launch promotions are uncontrolled.
demand_evidence.negative_evidence: GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5, DeepSeek-R1 and GPT-OSS all have more total comments than Jev. R1 also has strong later-window discussion, so resurgence is not unique to decision models. 179 of Jev's 252 threads have no comments. Jev activity has multiple peaks, not monotonic growth.
demand_evidence.dimensions: Same-scale daily posts and comments for all six models, plus a main-text table of D0, total posts/comments, and D4–D7 shares. Later share is distribution, not retention or a synthetic popularity index.
demand_evidence.gateway_scope: Vercel's original first-24-hour adoption chart, attributed and not digitized. Near 13% refers to paid Gateway teams trying Jev, not necessarily paying for Jev. Free promotion until September 25 confounds adoption. Raw denominators/hourly data and retention not established.
demand_evidence.prior_pain: A developer retrospectively describes a 2024 classifier/data-cleaning burden. Anecdote of a pre-existing need, not a representative survey or matched-quality ROI benchmark.
demand_evidence.conclusion: Supports rapid experimentation around a pre-existing semantic-judgment problem. Does not establish market-wide long-awaited demand satisfied, retention, willingness to pay, or causal superiority over generative models.
demand_evidence.next_evidence: Post-promotion usage, 7/30-day retention, paying use cases and incremental gains over existing classifiers.

reading_layout.policy: Core narrative, comparisons, market data, model explanations, evidence limits and adoption conclusions are ordinary visible prose, not clickable accordions. Only optional reproduction, inventory, loader diagnosis and skill details are collapsed. At the user's request, scenario plans and demo practices are popup-only rather than duplicated prose.
reading_layout.playground_disclosures: The policy/fixture/JSON inspector has moved to the optional #jev-model-lab within Jev integration. Live arena/support settings and dynamic records remain attached to their demos. Static practice notes open from cards below each demo.
reading_layout.presentation: Curated v1 deck: title + 18 substantive topic slides + two dedicated live-demo slides + closing (22 total), replacing 103 auto-split pages. presentation-outline.js provides bilingual editorial summaries linked to canonical sources; runtime presentation.js removes source slide markers only, leaving reading content/controls intact. No setup/audit-only or isolated chapter-intro pages. Each core demo has a dedicated slide containing the original interactive UI, reparented without cloning and restored on exit. Introduction links advance to that slide; manual Start and consent remain required, with no automatic inference. Entering/exiting preserves reading and disclosure state.
reading_layout.presentation_validation: examples/presentation-curation.json: browser deck accepted after full bilingual/mobility checks. Both 20-page PPTX/PDF exports were rendered, but Chinese conversion loses CJK glyphs and English uses substituted font styling; export typography is NOT accepted as deliverable. The later 22-page export also omits the live canvas and overlaps collapsed support content. Shared exporter/font/visibility issues are reported separately; interactive browser presentation is the accepted surface.
reading_layout.styles: reading.css and presentation.css are article-local; no global accordion behavior is changed.

category_analysis.definition: Models whose main output is bounded judgments, levels or distributions consumed directly by software. Analytical scope, not a standardized taxonomy; not every JSON-generating model has the same computation or training.
category_analysis.role: A semantic judgment component between data and deterministic workflow policy/execution, not a complete agent or authorization system.
category_analysis.value_hypothesis: Avoid unnecessary generation, repeated context and manual filtering; improve composability and traceability. Adoption requires a net benefit at matched quality after judgment, operations and error-recovery costs.
category_analysis.market_boundary: AI Index 2025 summarizes surveyed-organization AI use: 78% in 2024 versus 55% in 2023. Anthropic observes automation patterns in 77% of 1M sampled first-party API records from August 2025, not 77% of firms or successful tasks. The >280-fold GPT-3.5-level inference-cost decline covers Nov 2022–Oct 2024, not these models' measured speedup. No standalone category TAM established.
category_analysis.publication_signal: Multiple public implementations signal developer interest in a shared problem, not equivalent quality, rapid-from-scratch development, customer adoption or proven ROI.

verified_model_scope: This model ID applies only to the Jev case study, not to the whole category.
research_mode: Public-document review plus versioned local MLX/arena experiments; no live paid inference benchmark
arena_ui_defaults: New matches default to unlimited simulation duration (duration_s:null); Start and cloud consent remain explicit. Elimination, manual Stop, viewer lease and per-decision error/deadline protections remain. Shot totals appear in header KPI cards and diagnostics, not a duplicate footer sentence.

arena_research_cycle.method: Supervised finite cycle: preregister split/limits/source hashes, collect development, bind review, freeze, holdout, explicit local shadow probes, evidence-based promotion or rejection. No unattended spend or auto-deployment.
arena_research_cycle.result: 16 search-only paired games, then 12 real Laya snapshot calls. Holdout v2/v3 both 2/4 elimination wins and two caps; v3 repeats more and searches longer. No v3 superiority claim. Fixed-readout certificate covers 22/115 holdout v3 snapshots (19.1%). Four development shadow calls could be skipped in replay; no observed action disagreement, but no independent live speedup test.
arena_research_cycle.decision: Keep bounded-gap-v1 as an explicit research invocation optimization, not live default. Diagnose loops/search overhead next, using fresh holdout seeds; old inspected holdout becomes development/regression.

local_optimization_series.work: Four candidate cycles plus one fixed confirmation: 28 CPU screens, 56 completed actual model episodes, 1220 real local requests and 402 actual certified skips. One interrupted episode's five calls remain in cost; completed episodes were not rerun during append-only continuation.
local_optimization_series.finding: Global anti-cycle changes increased deaths. Conditional stagnation rescue improved known development cases for both checkpoints; fresh holdout and two-map confirmation tied baseline and never triggered rescue. Strict out-of-sample superiority is not established.
local_optimization_series.decision: No best-state or global-optimality claim, no automatic live strategy promotion. Stop this finite series; further optimization needs a new hypothesis and fresh test set. Build-scoped cache parity and bounded-score invocation are independently tested runtime techniques.

local_decision_models.architecture: One frontend/Node gateway, isolated NanoJev and Laya worker processes. Four explicit local model IDs; no provider fallback or weight replacement.
local_decision_models.scenarios: Basic Playground, support routing and arena share the catalog. Both Laya checkpoints support opponent-rollout planner ranking and raw choices. Normal arena UI defaults to planner/step/v7; raw input tests unassisted choice. Search-only isolates model-ranking contribution; rule attack is only a simple-policy sanity check. Removed modes remain historical/API compatibility, not new-match menu options. Unadapted Laya utility-attack/tactics remain rejected.
local_decision_models.strategy_revision: exchange-aware-v5: same side-relative HP+shield exchange utility for both teams, terminal outcome handling and 70% worst/30% mean response aggregation. Favorable mutual loss is allowed; forced progress attacks may not worsen the best risk-adjusted exchange. Retains v4 persistent goals/routes and interrupts route continuation on material health-balance changes. Native Boolean, Noul and online self-scores retain distinct adapter provenance. Earlier revisions remain explicit; no equilibrium or global-optimality claim.
local_decision_models.health_exchange_validation: examples/health-exchange-validation.json: side-swap payoff and mapping tests, dual-side three-adapter fixtures, 32 tokenizer-only inputs per tested checkpoint (max 483 tokens), and eight real local fixed-state checks across two checkpoints/two sides/ahead-behind states. No cloud calls or full-battle quality claim; four ahead cases had a singleton application-selected shortlist.
local_decision_models.persistent_intent_validation: examples/persistent-intent-validation.json: initial verbose NanoJev input rejected before inference; compact complete contract passed 16 tokenizer-only payloads per tested checkpoint. Two real model requests, one per NanoJev FP32/Laya typed-decisions, each followed by a two-tank route continuation without new search/inference. Separate from v3 research quality evidence.
local_decision_models.hull_rendering_fix: Chassis and parallel tracks rotate together using actual move history; turret aim is independent, HUD labels remain upright. Rendering-only change, desktop/mobile verified.
local_decision_models.tactical_wait_validation: examples/arena-tactical-wait-validation.json: 11 development tests, four eight-round search-only smoke matches, 64 tokenizer-only payloads per checkpoint; zero model/cloud forwards. Short smoke selected no waits; a separate development scene verifies beneficial wait admission.
local_decision_models.strategy_validation: examples/arena-strategy-validation.json: seven development fixture tests, 32 tokenizer-only inputs per checkpoint, zero new forwards. Earlier four real planner requests were v1 only.
local_decision_models.runtime: Dedicated laya-mlx 0.2.0 / MLX 0.32.2 environment, FP16; reuse existing multilingual and typed-decisions downloads. Pinned manifests and all listed files verified; startup is offline.
local_decision_models.limits: Reject question, option and state truncation before inference; full sequence <=1024 tokens, Choice <=20 options. Confidence/calibration and per-question token scopes remain distinct from NanoJev.
local_decision_models.scheduling: All managed local GPU requests share a FIFO lane in this Node process; arena alternates pair order. Submitted GPU work is not preemptible. Unrelated oMLX/other-server workloads are outside this scheduler.
local_decision_models.evidence_boundary: Initial six-request smoke is preserved separately. Follow-up: 192 tokenizer-only payloads per checkpoint, then four one-decision local planner requests, all contracts passed and none changed its same-side search-only plan. No cloud, retries or training. Defaults are not proven optimal; schema success and individual timings do not establish tactical, accuracy or hybrid gains.

role: Typed semantic judgments over bounded answer spaces, implemented by hosted or local models; application code owns exact rules, authorization and execution. Validate each implementation rather than inferring capabilities from the category name.
appropriate_uses: Semantic ticket classification with explicit review fallback
Model or skill selection from known candidates
Advisory tool-risk screening in addition to deterministic authorization
RAG passage relevance, contradiction, and citation-support checks
Batch document feature extraction with queues and rate limiting
not_a_replacement_for: Exact arithmetic, counting, date comparison, SQL, or deterministic rules
Free-text or code generation and general long-horizon planning
Authentication, authorization, sandboxing, or human approval
OCR, speech recognition, embedding index, durable workflow execution
Artifact/runtime compatibility checks or contractual privacy guarantees

constraints: Use criteria, not invented options/min/max fields.
Question IDs are not visible to model inference; instructions must stand alone.
Questions share state and are evaluated independently, not sequentially.
Choice/Score confidence summarizes the distribution, not probability of correctness.
Noul has no separate confidence field.

dated_limits.input: Text only, including structured JSON state
dated_limits.context_longest: 32k tokens: state plus the longest question
dated_limits.warning: Rate limits are dynamic; recheck the official models page. English is the primary training language.

design_requirements: Compare deterministic rules, supervised classifiers, Jev, and structured-output LLM baselines.
Enumerate other/none/unknown where the candidate set is not exhaustive.
Keep precision calculations and authorization in code.
Fail closed or route to review on errors, uncertainty, or destructive actions.
Calibrate thresholds on held-out task and language data; never copy example thresholds as guarantees.
Pin model, SDK and question/policy configuration; re-evaluate changes.
Measure end-to-end quality, calibration, automation coverage, tail latency, retries and total cost.
Minimize input and logs; no customer-data training does not imply zero retention.
agent_expected_deliverables: Adopt/reject recommendation with alternatives and evidence
Evaluation dataset plan, risk metrics and threshold acceptance criteria
requires_explicit_user_approval: Install skills or dependencies into a project
Create credentials or call billable APIs
Transmit real sensitive or private data
Execute business writes or change production configuration
revalidate_on: Changed questions, criteria, candidate set or policy
New language, domain or input distribution
Changed price, quota, hosting or data-processing terms

playground.mode: Live evaluation through a same-origin local backend; synthetic fixtures require an explicit separate action
playground.visible_output: Input and an always-visible output panel are paired. Explicit idle/running/completed/failed/cancelled/invalidated states are separate from service readiness. Successful calls show three answers and backend-normalized result JSON immediately. Policy suggestions live in an optional collapsed section; demo/import provenance stays explicit. Mobile runs reveal the output panel.
playground.readiness_scope: Read-only GET /v1/credits authentication probe, never model inference. Validates the response shape but does not expose balances. A pass does not prove Jev access, billing eligibility, or payment-method verification. Explicit credit-card-required 403 responses are classified separately from invalid credentials, unrelated forbidden responses, and insufficient credits.
playground.payment_method_boundary: When Gateway explicitly requires a valid credit card on file, the user must review Billing / Payment Method for the API key's owning team. Do not add cards, upgrade plans, buy credits, or assume promotional pricing waives account verification.
playground.secret_entry: --prompt-key uses hidden terminal input with no history or file storage; do not paste a multiline shell block into an interactive read command.
playground.runtime: Node.js >=22. Local routes use the isolated Python/MLX service documented below; Vercel SDK is not required. Optional cloud route: AI SDK 7.0.107 and @ai-sdk/gateway 4.0.87 installed outside the repository.
playground.gateway_mapping: boolean.probability maps to Noul; independent confidence comes only from providerMetadata.typesafe.confidence; Score legend comes from the request. Missing values remain null, not synthesized.
playground.live_measurements: Backend upstream round-trip latency, browser round-trip latency, and provider-reported input/output tokens; not GPU-only time, benchmark accuracy, or verified billing
playground.authentication_test_status: Cloud key/SDK configuration and read-only authentication do not prove model access. Successful cloud Jev inference remains unestablished. Both local MLX weight profiles have completed real GPU inference, HTTP checks, and same-weight numerical validation; these are not accuracy benchmarks.
playground.local_mapping: states[].answers Boolean p_true maps to Noul. Choice/Score confidence stays null. Tokens count actual candidate paths with repeated prefixes; output 0 means no autoregressive decoding. Defaults to FP32 when ready, otherwise local 4-bit; never falls back after an evaluation failure.
playground.metrics: Synthetic automation coverage and error rate among automated cases, never Jev benchmark accuracy
playground.input_edits: Invalidate previous results, cancel waiting, and discard late responses; threshold changes do not make new inference calls
playground.response_import: Checks normalized response shape, optional finite distributions with declared rounding, choice argmax, and Score consistency. Import never becomes a live API receipt or verifies model identity.
playground.privacy: Cloud keys remain in server environment variables. Local model-service tokens stay in owner-only 0600 cache files, never the browser. Local inference needs only an explicit Run click, not a checkbox. Cloud consent is revocable and retained separately per route in page memory until reload; input edits do not reset it. No input persistence or automatic inference; loopback binding, origin/CSRF checks, body limits, deadlines and rate limits. Not a public authenticated deployment.

laya_research.section_scope: Five bilingual substeps. References 52–55 are the historical public-document/code review and third-party arithmetic; reference 67 separately records the September 23 local integration. Do not relabel historical results as our inference.

checkpoints.scope: Multilingual base; a candidate for Chinese evaluation

laya_research.author_benchmark_boundary: 400 cases / 2,000 judgments. Base English 36.1%, multilingual 34.2%, tuned 76.6%, majority 46.1%. Jev 72.7% is a cited external baseline, not rerun alongside Laya; samples and prompts differ. No general superiority claim.
laya_research.community_recalculation: 40 paired Chinese single-label records: Jev 31/40, Laya multilingual MLX 23/40. Mean recorded times 588.325 and 7.2925 ms. Small sample, disputed labels; local model loading excluded and API network included. Requested Jev alias, returned revision absent; Laya HF revision unpinned. Not our inference, remote attestation, multi-label/order-binding accuracy, or NanoJev comparison.
laya_research.cascade_boundary: Threshold 0.60 was swept on the same 40 records: 22 escalations, 31 correct. Post-hoc replay, not independent held-out or freshly measured online hybrid gains.
laya_research.mlx_boundary: Independent port. Author M3 Max short single-question FP16 P50: 13.42/7.39 ms, loading excluded. 378/378 is selected-answer parity, not business accuracy. These historical author results are not the separate local integration in local_decision_models.
integration_requirements: Pin weights, runtime, language/checkpoint selection and temperature settings; no hidden auto-routing.
Validate full sequence budgets before upstream question/option/state truncation; preserve negation, later orders and counterevidence.
Confidence is not correctness probability; calibrate on separate data and preserve errors and abstention coverage.
Compare raw judgments with rules/classifiers and accessible hosted Jev on the same tasks, without LLM answer repair.
Explicit approval is required before installing dependencies, downloading/running weights or calling cloud inference.

architecture: Each state/question/candidate is a separate token path; one backbone call batches those paths.
Last EOS representation, LayerNorm, shared scalar head, optional set attention for Choice only.
Boolean uses one semantic path and logits [0,z]; Score returns the expected ordered level.
Reference inference repeats prefixes. One forward call does not imply shared state computation or constant candidate cost.

training_interpretation.status: Independent RLCD-inspired candidate, not a recovered TypeSafe training recipe
training_interpretation.paired_reward: For independent draws and an independent observed event: E[R] = 2 p.q - ||p||^2. The paired policy-gradient estimator targets the expected Brier gradient.
training_interpretation.do_not_infer: Unbiased raw gradients do not establish optimizer equivalence, empirical calibration, or superiority. Actions that change the outcome violate the simple independent-event premise.

navigation_evidence.source: Project-author community evaluation, not an independent rerun by this report
navigation_evidence.checkpoint: v3_teacher_coords_multi_seed17 (teacher-distribution training, not the paired-reward event checkpoint)
navigation_evidence.limitations: One checkpoint/seed; systems differ in training, head and input. Videos are replays, may be outcome-selected, and synchronize environment steps, not latency. Source-file consistency is not independent proof of remote inference.

event_probability_evidence.metric: Squared L2 to simulator-known event probabilities q, not accuracy, ECE, or observed-outcome Brier
event_probability_evidence.limitations: One seed and narrow events; 64 OOD Snake questions all have q(true)=1. Direct Brier wins on OOD NLL. No general method ranking established.

deployment.device: Current DecisionPredictor rejects non-CUDA devices; no built-in CPU or Apple MPS fallback
deployment.size_evidence: Six required root-checkpoint files were verified against pinned public sizes and hashes; reused the already-downloaded weights. Not a minimum-memory estimate.
deployment.checkpoint_selection: Root is the older navigation/initialization model. Choose local_atomic_seed17 for its local-maze setup, games_gold_seed17 for Snake, or the matched event-control variant.
deployment.max_length: Read from the checkpoint configuration; oversized candidate paths fail without silent truncation
api_gaps: Use boolean, not noul; map response p_true to Noul's yes probability.
Choice/Score omit native confidence and Score legend. Do not invent confidence from max probability; identify request-derived labels as such.
Instructions/criteria currently require nonempty strings; object state uses Python str representation, not canonical JSON.
A changed serialization is a changed model input; version and re-evaluate it.
Add authentication, workload limits, queueing and path redaction before public deployment.
deployment.playground_status: Upstream CUDA service was not deployed. A separate native MLX service is implemented, numerically verified, and integrated with original FP32 and quantized 4-bit profiles. No recorded or synthetic fallback.

nanojev_research.licensing: Repository code MIT; Qwen base Apache-2.0. The pinned HF card has no license field and no standalone LICENSE was found. Confirm fine-tuned-weight, dataset and teacher API terms before commercial use.

name_collision.differences: Separate implementation: Noul is an abstention slot, Score is Gaussian mean/std; not TypeSafe's Noul and ordered-Score semantics. No LICENSE found. Its performance claims were not adopted.

checks_executed_here.tokenizer: Initial stdlib tests used a character tokenizer. Subsequent real-weight MLX/PyTorch comparisons used the actual pinned tokenizer with exact candidate-token agreement.
checks_executed_here.formula_check: Independent M=2 enumeration for K=2,3,5; reward/gradient identities, not a full PyTorch training verification
checks_executed_here.request_example: examples/nanojev-request.json (validated against the pinned upstream validator)

local_mlx_audit.scope: Historical read-only artifact/installed-oMLX audit. Its no-load/no-inference flags describe that audit only; see native_mlx_runtime for later successful standalone inference.
local_mlx_audit.download_integrity: All 9 published files match sizes and Git/LFS hashes; no missing release files in the audited oMLX directory.
blockers: Discovery can see *.safetensors, but the selected chat loader uses model*.safetensors and misses best.safetensors.
Root config is a training record; architecture and tokenizer are in subfolders, with no root model_type or quantization configuration.
backbone.* and .weight.scales/.weight.biases need explicit mapping to the chosen MLX graph and per-module quantization; do not quantize the fp16 decision heads blindly.
A Qwen3 hidden-state forward plus norm, scalar, set_project, set_attention and set_output must be implemented, preserving input construction, final valid EOS, padding, candidate grouping and log(K).
Standard chat generation produces vocabulary logits and decoding, not the required typed decision API. oMLX needs dedicated engine/protocol support or an independently served decision runtime.
local_mlx_audit.shape_correction: Actual q_proj packed U32 shape is [2048,128], with [2048,16] scales/biases. The model card's packed [2048,16] example is a documentation error, not a reason to alter matching weights.
do_not_do: Do not redownload or rename files as a substitute for runtime implementation.
Do not use strict=False to discard trained decision heads or treat backbone model_type=qwen3 as the complete architecture.
Do not interpret lm_head absence as a missing download; tied embeddings may omit it.
Do not fetch the author's private training paths from config.json; they are not inference dependencies.
Do not equate author-reported dequantized agreement, file size, or matmul throughput with native MLX decision quality, memory, or latency.
next_steps: Standalone MLX forward, strict weight loading, bounded authenticated service, and playground integration are now implemented.
Same-weight MLX/PyTorch numerical comparisons passed for both profiles; quantization versus original FP32 has observable differences.
Domain accuracy, calibration, representative latency and broader numerical coverage remain to be validated.
If integrating into oMLX, add discovery, a decision engine and an evaluation endpoint; clear cached load failures only after the runtime is actually compatible.
local_mlx_audit.licensing: The quantized artifact declares no separate weight license; confirm upstream and derivative terms before production use.

native_mlx_runtime.status: Implemented and exercised on Apple Silicon, 2026-09-19; not an oMLX chat-engine modification
native_mlx_runtime.numerical_scope: 4 states / 12 questions / 28 paths. Real tokenizer, unchanged pinned upstream PyTorch DecisionModel, strict loading. Numerical fidelity only; not business accuracy, calibration, or bitwise equality.
native_mlx_runtime.quantized_vs_original_argmax_flips: 3 of 12 questions; not a population estimate
native_mlx_runtime.business_example: Both profiles really chose other for the public HTTP-500 routing example. These outputs are preserved, not corrected to technical. The root navigation checkpoint is not established as a reliable business classifier.
native_mlx_runtime.cost_scope: No external model API charge; excludes hardware, electricity, and maintenance
native_mlx_runtime.remaining: Business evaluation/calibration, broader parity and performance tests, weight licensing clarification. Dedicated oMLX engine/protocol support is a separate optional project.

after_sales_comparison.architecture_left: Explicit handoff/safe branch-memory reuse, otherwise one batch of independent Boolean intent/order propositions (5/9/13 questions). Confirmed branches receive separate policy actions. Model uncertainty is not treated as missing customer information: an explicit internal LLM review uses actual messages/known orders and must preserve locked branches. Only genuinely missing/ambiguous information warrants customer clarification. Unique requested single-order slots resume workflow memory. Review-derived decisions retain LLM provenance; raw native scores/plans and native-only checks remain visible. No multiple-issue or missing-order bypass of semantic recognition. Explanation-only LLM returns reply without re-deciding branches. rules_llm disables native inference for ablation.
after_sales_comparison.architecture_right: Same requested LLM, compact complete policy and history, with reply-first branches[{intent,order_id,action}] output; not a forced single other/human_review for multiple issues. Actual reply deltas stream before final schema validation.
after_sales_comparison.dataset: Seeded synthetic 1–3 cases / 3 turns each, including same-order multi-intent, different orders, ambiguous associations, negation, handoff and explanation. Gold branch sets stay out of model inputs. Not real customers or general accuracy evidence.
after_sales_comparison.fairness: Same customer inputs/facts, requested LLM and streaming transport. Per-question p_true >=0.8 is experimental support, <=0.2 absence, otherwise uncertainty; no cross-label softmax, top-two margin or multiplication. These are uncalibrated gates, not correctness guarantees. Rules/templates are application assistance. Unknown candidate labels are not asserted as user needs. Both see paired turns; per-side quota waits remain in latency. Do not relabel earlier measurements as v5. Semantic review calls count in full latency/usage and are not fast paths.
after_sales_comparison.reasoning_boundary: Both LLM paths use CLI --stream on with actual message_delta events relayed by authenticated SSE. No reasoning/tool/subagent events are exposed. Partial reply text is a draft until final validation; rejected/cancelled drafts stay labeled. Templates return atomically without fake typing. CLI still starts fresh sessions; no persistent SDK/direct-API speedup is claimed. Reasoning settings are provider-default.
after_sales_comparison.measurements: Backend reply latency includes all model/workflow stages and per-side admission wait; wait breakdowns are not double-added. Total Token sums reported input/output across native and LLM stages, including failures/cancellation; native/LLM subtotals are separate. Missing usage stays unknown. Cache/reasoning counts are not double-added. Different tokenizers/scopes prevent treating totals as dollars or proof of equal-quality savings.
after_sales_comparison.quality: Exact intent sets, order bindings and per-branch actions are checked, with missing/extra labels and clarification counts. Rule-only unevaluated fields are null. Known branches are preserved when others are uncertain, but clarification is not resolution. Five real FP32 development probes yielded all 53 scores in the uncertain band; they do not validate checkpoint multi-intent capability. Original scores were not threshold-tuned into successes. See tests/experiments/jev-support-multi-intent.md. Natural-language quality still needs review.
after_sales_comparison.controls: Explicit Start and cloud consent, cleared on settings changes. At most 9 native / 18 top-level LLM requests for 3 customers, plus CLI-internal work. Per-stage deadline 30/60/120 seconds, five-second viewer lease, 15-minute wall cap, Stop and no automatic retries/provider substitution; semantic uncertainty review is an explicit workflow branch, not a transport-error fallback. Mutually exclusive with arena/probe/other inference.
after_sales_comparison.verification: v5 screenshot regression uses injected all-uncertain native evidence to verify real streaming review, known-order preservation, locked-branch validation, memory reuse and honest usage/source accounting; no new cloud inference or checkpoint improvement is claimed. Earlier verification: injected multi-branch fixtures, 720 offline tokenizer cases (max 201/path, 2562/request), actual installed-CLI streaming against a loopback mock, plus five real local FP32 development probes with negative semantic evidence. No cloud inference, model training or general accuracy/speed advantage is claimed.
after_sales_comparison.business_actions: None: synthetic order ledger, no real refunds, writes or transfers.

arena_best_practices.scope: Project engineering experience, not vendor claims or a universal optimal strategy. No combat weight training is claimed.
recommendations: Define goals, units, feasible actions, execution feedback and versioned rules before refining prompts.
Compute geometry, arithmetic and constraints in code; disclose input assistance and retain raw-task controls.
Keep native Boolean utilities, online 0..100 self-preferences and application search values separate; none is established as calibrated win probability.
Batch by team but evaluate joint action consequences, resource conflicts and time-dependent friendly firing lanes.
Use fixed-state probes and paired synchronous maps before realtime trials; include search, inference, queueing and state age in timing.
Compare rule baseline, search-only and the same search plus model; retain losses, capped runs and negative model contribution.
Use explicit consent, strict score validation, cancellation and auditable failures without hidden provider/task fallback.
For irreversible business actions, add explicit execution-time state/permission checks; do not mistake a bounded forecast for an authorization or safety guarantee.
arena_best_practices.evidence_boundary: v6 sync: old survival+FP32 3/6 wins, search-only 6/6, search+FP32 6/6; model scoring reduced final HP in the two differing holdout cases. Four v6 realtime wins are small-sample observations. These do not transfer to v7 or cloud models; later v7/online compatibility checks use physics or injected responses.
current_limitations: Only the joint root action is executed; continuation uses simple policies and a 24-tick horizon.
A side still waits for all its living tanks' actions before requesting again.
Persistent shared targets, multi-turn roles, per-tank-ready scheduling and a trained combat value head remain future work.
arena_best_practices.publication_boundary: Public summary only; private raw receipts and credentials are not published. Summary consistency alone is not independent proof of model execution.

evidence_gaps: No independently reproduced neutral Jev benchmark was verified in this research.
No public weights, reproducible full RLCD training recipe or parameter count established by reviewed sources.
No project-specific Chinese accuracy, calibrated thresholds, production SLA or end-to-end savings measured.
No consistently defined standalone structured-decision-model market size verified; adjacent adoption and API-use data are not category market share.
No complete matched-task comparison of Jev, NanoJev and Laya; hosted access, local fidelity and task quality remain separate checks.
